\captionof{figure}{Three core results separating internal model judgment from exogenous execution authority. \textbf{(a)} Across proposer search widths $K_{\mathrm{opt}} \in [1, 4,096]$ (120,000 kernel episodes), internal transcript and learned guards collapse to $100\%$ breach via $1-(1-J)^{K_{\mathrm{opt}}}$ while the Verus-verified exogenous sink holds at $0.0\%$ (slope $0.0000$/doubling). \textbf{(b)} In 412-parameter policy-gradient training under audited tournament rewards, raising pre-commit sink mediation above $q_{\mathrm{gate}} \ge 0.75$ reverses the incentive for covert unmonitored shortcutting from $+34.5$\,pp to $+0.03$\,pp ($0.0\%$ harm) while lifting useful task completion from $61.5\%$ to $85.9\%$. \textbf{(c)} On live multi-step Qwen3-4B/8B AgentDojo tasks, static per-call symbolic policies (Progent) block single-call injections yet suffer $12.5\%$ cumulative budget breaches, whereas stateful exogenous mediation achieves $0.0\%$ breaches ($0/112$ pooled live runs, exact Suissa--Shuster $p = 1.9\times 10^{-9}$) and the highest safe-and-useful completion ($33.3\%$).}\label{fig:v5hero}
